## Introduction

::: {.notes}
A `.notes` block is the workhorse here: Quarto renders it as ordinary prose on
the website and as speaker notes on the slides (press `s` in the deck).

Consecutive paragraphs can share one block.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
Content for the slides only goes in a `.content-visible when-format="revealjs"` block.

-   a bullet summary for the slide
-   which would be redundant on the page
:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
Content for the website only goes in a `.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"`
block.
:::

## You decide when slide breaks happen

::: {.notes}
Each `##` heading starts a slide. To split content across two slides, you
must repeat the heading, but this can look awkward on the website, so keep
the repeat short or move it into a `revealjs`-only block.
:::

```{r}
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
```

## You decide when slide breaks happen

```{r}
plot(mtcars$hp, mtcars$mpg)
```

## Revealing content step by step

::: {.notes}
Reveal things in sequence with reveal.js's own tools: `. . .` for a pause, or a
`.fragment` / `.incremental` block. These are ignored on the website, so they are
safe to leave in the shared text.
:::

A first point.

. . .

A second point, one advance later.

::: {.incremental}
-   then this
-   then this
:::

## Handling a long slide

::: {.notes}
Because nothing shrinks content for you, use per-slide classes when a
slide overflows: `## Heading {.smaller}` shrinks the text, and
`## Heading {.scrollable}` lets that one slide scroll.
:::

::: {.smaller .content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
This slide is a good candidate for `{.smaller}` since the code and its output
would not fit otherwise.

```{r}
head(mtcars[, 1:4], 30)
```
:::

## Callouts

::: {.notes}
Callouts keep their boxes on the slides, and reveal.js renders callout text
smaller than slide text. A `collapse="true"` callout is *not* collapsible in a
deck -- Quarto only honours that in HTML -- so on the slide the content is simply
visible. If you want to hide a solution until you advance, wrap it in a
`.fragment` block yourself.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## A note
Visible in both outputs, box and all.
:::

:::: {.callout-caution}
## An exercise solution
::: {.fragment}
Wrapped in a `.fragment`, so it appears on the next advance in the deck while
staying plain prose on the website.
:::
::::
